the proposed approach allows for a fast and monotonic learning convergence of the presented nonlinear ILC for multi-input, multivariable nonlinear time-varyng systems.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: 1) the design of the nonlinear I LC for a class of multi-input, multi output nonlinear time-varyng systems with the use of a simulation-based design approach for learning gains tuning to achieve monotonic convergence of ILC; 2) the simulation-based tuning of the feedback controller for the nonlinear ILC to achieve fast and accurate tracking; 3) the experimental validation of the proposed approach for the nonlinear I LC of a real robot manipulator.
the design and analysis of the nonlinear model-based ILC and its tuning by using the simulation-based approach.
simulation-based tuning of learning and feedback gains for monotonic convergence of ILC for nonlinear systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented simulation-based approach is the only possible solution for practical online tuning for monotonic learning process.
the presented ILC algorithm has a potential for practical implementation in real industrial applications.
the simulation-based tuning is a very powerful and effective tool to achieve the monotonic convergence of nonlinear ILC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simulation-based approach is a very powerful technique for the design of nonlinear ILC for nonlinear systems.
the proposed approach can be used to achieve monotonic convergence in the case of non-monotonic learning.
the presented approach is a good compromise between the classical engineering approach and the modern model-based approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the monotonic convergence of ILC is achievable in a simulation-based approach.
the simulation-based tuning of learning gains is a necessary step in the design of model-based ILC for nonlinear time-vary ing systems.
a monotonic convergence of ILC can be achieved by using a simulation-based design and the proposed approach can be used for tuning learning and feedback gains for any model-based nonlinear ILC.
